problems.statement: The count-based 20-closes-per-day quota, enforced with leaderboard consequences, rewards gaming (premature solves, ticket splitting, cherry-picking quick wins), which inflates closes while creating reopens, split children and duplicates that grow the backlog.

Real first-contact demand barely changed (+4%); the ticket-volume surge is self-generated: split children rose from 240 to 3,710 and customer duplicates from 410 to 2,770 per month, so the backlog is mostly artifacts of the quota.

Complex tickets are being starved: agents skip them in favor of quick-wins, so complex aged tickets rose from 140 to 430 and the oldest-first pick share fell from 71% to 34%, and customers like Larkspur get bounced solves and churn risk.
The Payroll launch flooded the queue and explains the backlog doubling.
Agents are not working hard enough or the target is too soft (VP's presented view).
A capacity shortfall (too few agents) is the cause; 12 extra agents would fix the backlog.
The reopen-rate rise is a measurement artifact from an auto-reopen-on-reply rule change.

Attrition and the competing Corvane pay offer, with the deferred pay review, are a material and growing threat (survey intent to leave 58% vs 21%), partly tied to quota pressure, but have not yet reduced capacity.

A real engineering backlog (support-escalated bugs 40 to 71, bank-feed API change) contributes to aged complex tickets, but its share is unquantified and it does not explain the split, duplicate or reopen explosion or the Billing-Compliance contrast.

Poor congruence between the work (complex, resolution-dependent), the formal organization (count-based quota, leaderboard, no credit for hard tickets, no outcome metric) and the informal norms (gaming, tricks passed along) drives the output gap.

causalClaims.from: Close quota with leaderboard and gameable counting rules
causalClaims.to: Splitting, premature solves and quick-win cherry-picking
Reopens, split children and customer duplicates inflating ticket creation and the backlog
Aging of complex tickets and falling CSAT

causalClaims.from: Banking-partner API change and engineering bug backlog
Counting reopened closes against the quota (Team C)

actions.action: Suspend the raw closes-per-day quota and leaderboard; replace with a balanced measure (first-contact resolution with no reopen in 14 days, complexity-weighted, oldest-first and aging targets, CSAT) without punishing agents for the transition.
actions.rationale: The established cause is the metric design, and this is reversible and cheap.

actions.action: Stop counting split children, reopened re-solves and duplicates as separate closes; restore oldest-first or SLA-based picking and retire or constrain the quick-wins filter.
actions.rationale: This directly removes the gaming levers and the self-generated ticket volume.

actions.action: Run a targeted cleanup: merge duplicates and split children into parent tickets, and assign experienced agents or a swarm to the aged complex and reopened tickets, starting with at-risk accounts such as Larkspur.
actions.rationale: About 2,780 of the 3,900 open tickets are reopened, split or duplicate artifacts, so merging can cut the backlog quickly and protect renewals.

actions.action: Tag and link aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs and set up a joint triage with Integrations, with proactive customer communication on the bank-feed issue.
actions.rationale: This quantifies the unknown engineering contribution cheaply and stops repeated tickets on known defects.

actions.action: Bring forward the deferred pay review or retention measures and stop using quota-miss leaderboards.
actions.rationale: Attrition risk is high with Corvane paying more, but its causal weight is not yet proven and cost is committed.

actions.action: Adopt a Team C style rule (reopened closes do not count) as an interim step.
actions.rationale: It cut reopens from 24% to 10% but left splitting and quick-win bias, so it is only a partial fix.

actions.action: Make the tougher target with real consequences the main lever (raise the 20, add penalties).
actions.rationale: It would intensify the gaming that created the problem, drive further attrition and worsen customer outcomes.

actions.action: Approve all 12 extra agents now ($744k per year, irrevocable within the fiscal year).
actions.rationale: Capacity was not the cause, and new hires under the same incentives would add more gamed volume; revisit after the metric is fixed.

actions.action: Reconsider headcount after 6 to 8 weeks of corrected metrics and a clean baseline of true demand, possibly a smaller staged request.
actions.rationale: Real residual capacity need is only measurable once the artificial volume is removed.

nextEvidence: Link aged complex tickets (430) and open backlog to open engineering bugs to quantify how much aging is waiting on engineering rather than on agent pick behavior.
Baseline of true workload after the metric change: first-contact issues, genuine reopens and net resolution per agent over 4-6 weeks, to size any real capacity gap before committing to headcount.

Per-agent and per-team data on gaming behavior (split rate, premature solves, quick-win share) and retention risk, to target coaching and test whether attrition is driven by quota pressure or by the Corvane pay gap.
output.summary: The backlog doubling is mostly self-inflicted. The count-based quota rewarded fast, shallow closes, so agents split tickets, solved prematurely and picked quick wins. Splits (240 to 3,710), duplicates (410 to 2,770) and reopens (6% to 23%) inflated volume while first-contact demand rose only 4%. The Billing-Compliance pod, with no quota, stayed stable. Payroll, capacity, effort and the reopen-rule change are rejected. The engineering bug backlog and Corvane attrition are live but unquantified. Replace the quota with outcome-based measures, clean up artifact tickets, swarm aged complex tickets, and defer the 12-agent request.
